name: GTT
product_focus: Managed SD-WAN, SASE/SSE, Envision, Tier 1 backbone
evidence_summary: GTT sources evidence managed SD-WAN, SASE/SSE, vendor-agnostic delivery, Envision platform and global Tier 1 backbone.
cost_model: Quote-based managed service; GTT public page answers cost only as consultative/requirement-based.
key_differentiators: Tier 1 global backbone provides strong international transit capability alongside managed SD-WAN.
Vendor-agnostic SD-WAN delivery (multiple platform options) with the Envision management platform.
Recognised as a leader for SASE and managed SD-WAN by industry analysts.
best_fit_for: Multinational enterprises needing strong international backbone alongside managed SD-WAN.
Buyers wanting platform flexibility within a managed service.
Organisations consolidating global transit, SD-WAN and SASE under one provider.
watch_outs: SASE depth depends heavily on the chosen platform partner; native SSE capabilities are not primary positioning.
Commercial model is consultative; ensure cost lines for managed changes, security and SLAs are explicit.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason stated. Sources found and rejected are listed in the evidence register at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: EtherVision portal analytics; platform AI depends on the chosen vendor mix.

resilience.note: Tier 1 backbone spanning 450+ PoPs with diverse routing.

profile.platform_architecture: GTT delivers managed SD-WAN and SASE over its global Tier 1 IP backbone (AS3257) spanning 450+ PoPs, with a multi-vendor platform bench and the EtherVision portal providing estate visibility. The model is network-led: GTT's internet backbone is the product, with managed services layered on top and last-mile aggregation handled globally.
profile.security_sase: GTT Secure Connect builds SASE outcomes on partner platforms (notably Fortinet and Palo Alto pairings) with managed security operations. Security depth follows the platform; GTT's contribution is backbone performance, global circuit aggregation and a single managed wrap across regions.
profile.service_support_channel: Fully managed and co-managed with 24x7 operations and named service management; UK and European delivery is established with US depth too. GTT positions sharply on price against the incumbent carriers, which resonates with cost-led multinational procurement.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-site managed pricing, quote based and typically aggressive. The Netify verdict: shortlist GTT when you want global managed SD-WAN with Tier 1 backbone performance at challenger pricing, particularly for internet-first designs across many countries. Buyers wanting deep first-party security IP or premium-brand service wrap should weigh trade-offs accordingly.

vendor_faqs.q: What does GTT's Tier 1 backbone mean for my WAN?
vendor_faqs.a: Your internet-first SD-WAN rides AS3257 with direct global peering rather than transit chains, which improves consistency for site-to-cloud and inter-region traffic without MPLS economics.

vendor_faqs.q: Is GTT cheaper than the big incumbents?
vendor_faqs.a: Frequently, yes: challenger positioning shows in like-for-like managed SD-WAN bids. Ensure service wrap, SLAs and in-country support match your expectations as part of the comparison.
A multi-vendor bench including Fortinet and VeloCloud lineages with SASE outcomes via partner SSE; GTT proposes against your estate with its backbone and aggregation as the constant.

shortlist_summary: GTT own a Tier 1 global backbone, which is the foundation for their managed SD-WAN positioning and gives strong international transit capability as a result. Typically shortlisted by organisations with a multinational estate where backbone ownership and international performance are scoring criteria, though it's worth confirming during evaluation how much of the delivery for your specific footprint runs over the GTT network versus public internet paths.
cost_note: Challenger pricing against incumbent carriers on like-for-like global managed SD-WAN, on a Tier 1 backbone.
uk_basis: UK contracting entity with UK operations on a Tier 1 backbone; UK and EMEA delivery is established.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: We manage the underlay (network) and the cloud-based overlay (SD-WAN) as a unified service
f01_fully_managed_service.note: GTT positions Managed SD-WAN as an end to end managed service covering circuit installation, hardware delivery, zero touch provisioning and 24/7/365 proactive monitoring under one bill and one support team. Corroborated by the GTT SD-WAN datasheet (register 18, Tier 3 host) which states GTT experts design, implement, install and optimise the service.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: GTT's Secure Co-Manage feature provides full security management capability that includes firewall policy and object management
f03_co_managed_service.note: Secure Co-Manage (GTT press release, 21 July 2021, register 14) lets customers make policy changes without placing an order while GTT continues to run the platform. The SASE Secure Connect page lists 'Access to co-management platform' and EnvisionDX states 'run operations in-house or collaborate with GTT's global experts'. Note the 2021 release names the legacy EtherVision portal; the current portal branding is Envision.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The GTT Channel Partners page, the Envision page and the EnvisionDX page were all checked for the exact strings 'multi-tenant' and 'white label' and both were ABSENT on each. The Channel Partners page only offers sell-to, sell-with or sell-through commercial models, which is not evidence of tenant isolation, delegated administration or branded partner portals.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Your Project Manager ensures the successful deployment of your complex solutions with well-defined milestones along the way.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: GTT publishes a structured Professional Services portfolio (Project Management, Technical Management, Service Management, Customer Incident Management, Program Management) aligned to PRINCE2 and ITIL. Graded partial because the exact string 'migration' was ABSENT on the Professional Services index, and no published discovery, pilot, staging, migration runbook, rollback plan or training detail was found.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Lifecycle operations for SD-WAN/SASE, internet, voice, cloud connect, plus performance tuning and change control
f07_lifecycle_management.note: GTT Envision advertises lifecycle operations and change control, and Professional Services covers 'throughout the lifecycle of your deployment'. Graded partial because exact string checks on the Managed SD-WAN page returned ABSENT for both 'firmware' and 'hardware replacement', and no published statement was found on patching, renewals or end of life planning being included in the service.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Dual SIM capability allows automatic switching between carrier networks during localized outages
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: GTT publishes a 5G Fixed Wireless Access service supporting primary and failover use ('Deploy automatic failover for primary circuits'), multi-carrier SIM handling, and feeding 'reliable underlay connectivity into SD-WAN and SASE architectures'. The Managed SD-WAN page lists access types 'fiber, broadband, 4G/5G'. Signal monitoring specifically was not evidenced.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: 100+ Points of Presence (POPs) between GTT and Palo Alto Networks for secure, edge-based access
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: GTT operates its own Tier 1 IP backbone PoPs, but the security enforcement edge is explicitly shared with Palo Alto Networks, and the 2021 launch release states the GTT SASE platform 'utilizes Palo Alto Networks Prisma Access'. The 2025 release describes a 'managed single-vendor SASE solution with Palo Alto Networks Prisma SASE'. Under the definition, gateways belonging to a third party whose technology the supplier resells grade partner_integrated rather than yes.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: The SASE Secure Connect page offers a dedicated private cloud option, restricted to the Fortinet variant. Exact string checks on the same page returned ABSENT for both 'sovereign' and 'on-premises', so customer-hosted or sovereign PoP deployment was not evidenced. Graded partial and the dedicated instance is a partner (Fortinet) construct rather than a GTT-built PoP.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: GTT owns and operates one of the world's largest global Tier 1 IP backbones
f21_private_global_backbone.note: GTT is a Tier 1 IP transit operator. The Fortinet press release (register 16) describes a 'top-ranked, global, Tier 1 IP backbone, which spans more than 260 cities on six continents', and the Connect page claims the '4th largest global IP backbone'. This is genuinely global rather than single-country, so yes rather than partial.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Choose the right Service Level Objective (SLO) to meet your operational needs.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The SASE page frames commitments as Service Level Objectives, not contractual SLAs, and also states '365/24/7 uptime assurance'. The Service Management page covers scheduled service reviews and SLA tracking. Graded partial because no published SLA schedule with contractual uptime, response or change-handling terms, or latency/jitter/loss commitments, was found on gtt.net; only a marketing stat of 99.99% network availability on the Connect page.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Powered by market-leading partners Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Firewalling is delivered as 'Firewall as a Service (FWaaS) – Provides cloud-based firewall protection for your network' but the underlying stack is third-party. The Fortinet release (16) lists ZTNA, FWaaS, CASB and SWG from Fortinet; the 2025 Palo Alto release (17) lists SD-WAN, FWaaS, SWG, CASB and ZTNA under Prisma SASE. GTT resells and manages rather than authors the NGFW, so partner_integrated.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: prevents sensitive data from being exposed or exfiltrated by identifying, monitoring, and
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: GTT's Cloud Security page lists 'Data Loss Protection (DLP)' as one of six SSE services, and the CASB page states it leverages data loss prevention technologies. Graded partner_integrated because the SSE stack is explicitly Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks technology per the SASE page. Alerting and exception workflow detail was not found. Quote is a verified substring of the DLP service description; the full sentence continues with enforcing policies on data across users, devices, applications, and networks.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: 24/7/365 support from NOC and SOC teams
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: GTT publishes both NOC and SOC coverage. The SD-WAN datasheet (register 18, Tier 3 host) states 24/7 continuous, proactive, end-to-end monitoring by global NOCs and SOCs, and the Service Management page provides an ITIL-accredited Service Manager, scheduled service reviews and SLA tracking. Formal root cause analysis wording was not directly quoted, though Customer Incident Management is a named service.

delivery_model.quote: We manage the underlay (network) and the cloud-based overlay (SD-WAN) as a unified service
delivery_model.note: GTT operates a network and a managed service wrap rather than authoring the SD-WAN or SSE product. The SASE service is 'Powered by market-leading partners Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks' and the 2025 press release describes a 'managed single-vendor SASE solution with Palo Alto Networks Prisma SASE'. GTT does own and operate its own Tier 1 IP backbone, which is infrastructure ownership rather than product authorship, so managed_provider rather than both.

underlay_ownership.quote: GTT owns and operates one of the world's largest global Tier 1 IP backbones
underlay_ownership.note: GTT owns the core Tier 1 IP backbone and routing (more than 260 cities on six continents per register 16), but last-mile access is procured on the customer's behalf: the Managed SD-WAN page states GTT handles the logistics of circuit installation across fibre, broadband and 4G/5G, and the 5G page describes wrapping multi-carrier 5G from other operators into a single managed service. Core owned, access largely resold, hence mixed.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Powered by market-leading partners Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks
sse_layer_ownership.note: Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. GTT's SASE/SSE stack is dual-vendor: the 2021 release states the GTT SASE platform utilises Palo Alto Networks Prisma Access, the 2025 release describes a managed single-vendor SASE solution with Palo Alto Networks Prisma SASE, and the 2024 release adds Fortinet-sourced ZTNA, FWaaS, CASB and SWG. GTT supplies the managed wrap, the backbone and 1,000+ Fortinet NSE-certified staff, not the security software.

regulatory_documentation.quote: GTT's SOC 2 scope includes the SD-WAN and SIP Trunking services.
regulatory_documentation.note: Found and named on GTT's security and compliance page: ISO 27001:2022 ('GTT holds ISO 27001: 2022 compliance at multiple locations, please view the certifications list for further information.'), SOC 1, SOC 2 scoped to SD-WAN and SIP Trunking, PCI DSS with an Attestation of Compliance available on request, GDPR, plus ISO 20000 and ISO 22301 at named operation centres and UK PSN at OFFICIAL. NOT found: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2, Cyber Essentials.

pop_count.quote: With 140,000+ customer sites connected and 400+ points of presence, you can enjoy reliable, consistent service wherever you operate with faster access and smoother collaboration
pop_count.note: The figure is published as '400+' so the true count is at least 400. This is the network PoP count. It conflicts with the SASE page, which claims '100+ Points of Presence (POPs) between GTT and Palo Alto Networks for secure, edge-based access', a different and smaller security edge footprint that is partly Palo Alto's. Recorded in conflicts.

sla_availability_pct.note: This figure appears as a benefit stat under the 'Resilient by design' comparison panel on the Connect page, not in a published SLA schedule. No availability percentage was found on the Managed SD-WAN or SASE Secure Connect pages; the SASE page uses Service Level Objective wording and '365/24/7 uptime assurance' with no number, and an exact string check for '99.9' on that page returned ABSENT. Treat 99.99 as a marketing claim rather than a verified contractual commitment.
